findings.title: The white flash stays on for good when the sim tick stops (duel loss by a hit, a pause, sector game over)
findings.claim: The flash is timed only by sim ticks counted from the tick the hit was seen. If the tick stops advancing within 2 ticks of the hit, `state.tick - flashTick` stays at 0 or 1 and the flash never turns off. In the duel this happens on every loss to a hit while the interior view is showing: the killing hit's `hitsCrew` event is drained on the frame after the last tick, stepping then stops, and the whole interior stays under the white flash (0.85 × 0.5) behind the end screen's translucent backdrop until Enter restarts. The same happens if the duel or the sector is paused (Esc or window blur) within 33 ms of a hit, and on the sector's last frame when a hit ends the run.
findings.evidence: interiorFeel.ts diff L933 `flashTick = state.tick` and L1000-1001 `flashAlpha(state.tick - flashTick, …)`; impactModel.ts diff L791-792 (the tick count is the only bound). app/duel/runtime.ts:217 `if (ended()) return;` stops stepping, and sim/duel/step.ts:126 `st.tick++` is the only place d.interior.tick moves. sim/tactical/duel.ts:38 sets EnemyWins when the crew ship goes down; render/tactical/fxModel.ts:35-36 `hitsCrew` matches that hit. duelMode.ts diff L44 passes the drained events into interior.draw. render/duel/endScreen.ts:29 draws the backdrop at `BACKDROP_ALPHA * 0.6`, so the interior shows through. The sector session freezes the tick while paused (session.ts diff L143). tests/interiorFeel.test.ts diff L2257-2260 tests the flash only with the tick advancing.
findings.why: Spec section 7 promises a 33 ms flash. In ordinary play (losing a duel while walking the interior, or alt-tabbing during combat) the interior instead stays washed out for the rest of the end screen or the pause. This is the look-and-feel check the owner will see.
findings.fix: Bound the flash by real time as well. On a hit, set `flashLeft = FLASH_TICKS / TICK_HZ` and decrease it by the real frame dt (add `realDt` to FeelFrame: the renderer's `dt`, and the duel's `dt` rather than `presentDt`). Show the flash only while `ticksSince < FLASH_TICKS && flashLeft > 0`. A hitstop still does not extend it. Add an interiorFeel test that holds `state.tick` fixed for 10 frames after a hit and expects the flash to be hidden.

findings.title: A pause freezes the shake offset (and any running hitstop) on screen
findings.claim: While paused the views pass a presentation dt of 0, so `stepShake` does not advance and `shakeOffset` keeps returning the last non-zero offset. The world (and in the sector, the projectiles and callouts) sits up to 6 art pixels off-centre for the whole pause. If a hitstop was running when the pause began, `clock.stopped` also stays true, so fire and arc animations stay frozen during the pause, against Decision 17's 'AnimatedSprites keep playing while paused'.
findings.evidence: renderer.ts diff L1813-1814 (`paused ? 0 : dt`, then `world.position.set(fit.x + shake.x, …)`); interiorView.ts diff L467-468; impactModel.ts diff L777-787 (stepShake holds at pdt 0, shakeOffset non-zero while left > 0); presentClock.ts diff L1564-1566 (`advance(0)` leaves `stop` untouched); plan L61 (Decision 17). The old sector shake decayed on the real dt (projectiles.ts diff L1694-1698). Task 8's review noted this.
findings.why: Cosmetic: a paused ship drawn slightly off-centre, and fire that stops flickering only when a pause lands inside a 60 ms hitstop. It is not blocking, but it is a small change from today's pause behaviour.
findings.fix: Pass a separate paused flag (or the real dt) into InteriorFeel.draw. While paused, either return a {0,0} shake or step the shake and the hitstop's remaining stop by the real dt, leaving the rest of the presentation clock held.

findings.title: Per-frame rebuilds and allocations in interiorFeel
findings.claim: Every frame, the composite clears and refills the starfield Graphics (68 rects), the vacuum Graphics and the fixtures Graphics. It also rebuilds every particle Source with fresh closures and key strings, spreads them into a new array, calls `consoles(state)` again (consoleLayer already calls it each frame), allocates the 68-object `stars` array and the `burning` array (with an O(n²) `includes`), and the sector side allocates `Int32Array.from` and `Uint8Array.from` for sectorHits and breachOpenings.
findings.evidence: interiorFeel.ts diff L965-966, L973, L977-978, L990-992, L1004-1005; lightsModel.ts diff L1107-1116; impactModel.ts diff L802; sources.ts diff L1488; renderer.ts diff L1811 and L1813.
findings.why: Small at today's ship sizes (the plan's 600-sprite preallocation already holds the display tree steady), but this is avoidable GC and geometry churn at 60 fps on top of the existing layers.
findings.fix: Later: cache stars per t-quantum or move them as sprites, reuse source objects keyed by tile, pass the consoles list from the view, and keep seen buffers that are reused rather than reallocated. Not needed before merge.

Hit timings: the shake is 6 art px decaying linearly over 0.25 s in whole art pixels × artPx = 2 × fit.scale (impactModel.ts diff L760-788). The hitstop is 0.06 s × feel, applied before advance so the hit frame's pdt is 0 (interiorFeel.ts diff L933, L958-959). The opening debris is spawned even at pdt 0 (L970). Smoke lasts 3 s per hit room in the sector, or on one floor tile picked by emitter.random in the duel (L940, L946).

The test checks no cell is covered twice and the union is unchanged on the Cutter and the Skiff (gradeModel.test.ts diff L2163-2182).
Performance: the 600 particle Sprites are created up front in particleLayer.ts (diff L1252), and 120 calm frames add no display objects (interiorFeel.test.ts diff L2227-2235).

Console desks are on the art-pixel grid: DESK_W 20, DESK_D 10, SCREEN_D 2, inset 2, outline 2 drawn inside (consoleModel.ts diff L276, L294-298; consoleLayer.ts diff L254), tested for every side and flush case (consoleModel.test.ts diff L1850-1862).
